courses.title: Physical Geography
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to the basic physical elements of geography and the diverse physical environment in which we live. Topics include the global patterns of weather and climate, landforms, soils and vegetation along with human modification of natural environments. The geographic tools used to explore these topics include maps, GPS, remote sensing and Geographic Information Systems (GIS).

courses.title: Cultural Geography
courses.description: The course will examine the location of people and activities throughout the world and analyze the reasons for their distribution. Topics discussed include population and migration, human-environment relationships, geographies of language, religion, race and ethnicity, economic activities, political organization and settlement patterns including the urban environment.

courses.title: A Geography of California
courses.description: This course is an exploration of California's diverse physical landscapes (land forms, climate, soil and resources) and analyzes its cultural landscapes created by human transformation of the environment through economic activities such as agriculture, mining, trade, industry and urbanization. It examines the remarkable physical and cultural regional differences within California, and studies the wealth of diversity of California's peoples while investigating the more disturbing aspects of discrimination and exploitation of various groups based on race, ethnicity, class and gender.

courses.title: Introduction to Geographic Information System
courses.description: This introductory course provides a foundation in the principles and applications of Geographic Information Systems (GIS). Students will learn how to acquire, manage, analyze, and visualize spatial data. Through hands-on exercises using industry-standard GIS software, students will develop practical skills in spatial data analysis, map creation, and problem-solving using a geographic perspective. This course will explore the fundamental concepts of spatial data models, geodatabases, spatial analysis techniques, and cartographic design, with applications across various disciplines.
courses.advisories: ENGL C1000 or ENGL C1000H or ESL D005. Pre-algebra or equivalent (or higher), or appropriate placement beyond pre-algebra

metadata.Transferability: Transferable to both UC and CSU
metadata.Advisory(ies): ENGL C1000 or ENGL C1000H or ESL D005. Pre-algebra or equivalent (or higher), or appropriate placement beyond pre-algebra
metadata.Student Learning Outcomes: Identify various GIS data sources, describe different data formats, and explain map projections and coordinate systems. Apply cartographic principles to design effective maps for data display and create online maps. Perform data management tasks to edit and store spatial and attribute data in geodatabases and query data based on spatial and attribute criteria. Utilize spatial data analysis tools to analyze patterns, perform geocoding, and demonstrate practical problem-solving. Apply GIS methodologies to solve real-world problems and evaluate the technology's limitations and ethical implications.
metadata.Course Description: This introductory course provides a foundation in the principles and applications of Geographic Information Systems (GIS). Through hands-on exercises using industry-standard GIS software, students will develop practical skills in spatial data analysis, map creation, and problem-solving using a geographic perspective. metadata.Course Philosophy: This Introduction to GIS course embraces a hands-on, problem-centered philosophy, empowering students to become proficient in spatial thinking and analysis. We believe in fostering a learning environment where students actively engage with real-world geospatial data, learn to apply GIS tools to solve practical problems, and develop critical thinking skills to interpret and communicate spatial information effectively. By bridging theory with practical application, we aim to cultivate adaptable learners who can leverage GIS to address challenges across diverse disciplines and contribute meaningfully to a data-driven society.

courses.title: World Regional Geography
courses.description: This course is an introduction to the major distinctive regions of the world, their natural environments, people, resources, agriculture, manufacturing, trade, cities, and the problems relating to contemporary society in each region. It seeks to investigate and analyze the increasing interdependencies among and between regions.

metadata.Student Learning Outcomes: Identify and apply geographic themes to describe the major geographic regions of the world. Explain and analyze the interaction and interdependence of physical and human landscapes in major geographic realms. Demonstrate understanding of the dynamics of population change, resource distribution, global economics and culture, and political conflicts in designated regions.

metadata.Course Philosophy: This course seeks to explore the world's regions by examining the interaction of the earth's physical or natural environment with its cultural environment. As students discover the unique characteristics of people and places in different geographic realms, they also develop an understanding and appreciation of the similarities between people and places.
